## Overview

The paper "Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks" was authored by Guangxuan Xiao and four other authors. The work was published as arXiv paper 2309.17453, and was presented at ICLR 2024.

## Problem Statement

Deploying LLMs in streaming applications poses two major challenges: firstly, caching previous tokens' Key and Value states (KV) consumes extensive memory during decoding, and secondly, popular LLMs cannot generalize to longer texts than the training sequence length.

## Key Discovery: Attention Sinks

Window attention, where only the most recent KVs are cached, is a natural approach—but it fails when the text length surpasses the cache size. The authors observed an interesting phenomenon, namely attention sink, that keeping the KV of initial tokens will largely recover the performance of window attention.

The emergence of attention sink is due to the strong attention scores towards initial tokens as a "sink" even if they are not semantically important.

## StreamingLLM Framework

StreamingLLM is an efficient framework that enables LLMs trained with a finite length attention window to generalize to infinite sequence lengths without any fine-tuning. StreamingLLM addresses memory issues by retaining only the most recent tokens and attention sinks, discarding intermediate tokens.

## Results and Applications

StreamingLLM can enable Llama-2, MPT, Falcon, and Pythia to perform stable and efficient language modeling with up to 4 million tokens and more. In streaming settings, StreamingLLM outperforms the sliding window recomputation baseline by up to 22.2x speedup.

Adding a placeholder token as a dedicated attention sink during pre-training can further improve streaming deployment.

## LazyEviction Paper Overview

LazyEviction is an observation window-based lagged eviction framework retaining latent recurring tokens by prioritized eviction based on tokens' recurrence patterns.

### Key Problem Addressed

The extended reasoning sequences in LLMs introduce significant GPU memory overhead due to increased key-value (KV) cache, with existing KV cache compression methods struggling in long reasoning tasks.

### Core Innovation

The paper analyzes attention patterns in reasoning tasks and reveals a Token Importance Recurrence phenomenon: a large proportion of tokens regain high attention after multiple decoding steps, which is failed to capture by existing works and may lead to unpredictable eviction on such periodically critical tokens.

### Performance Results

LazyEviction reduces KV cache by 50%~70% while maintaining comparable accuracy, outperforming existing KV cache compression baselines.

### Implementation Details

LazyEviction contains two key components: (1) Recurrence Interval Tracking for capturing temporal variations in token importance, and (2) a Maximum Recurrence Interval-Centric Eviction Policy that prioritizes eviction based on tokens' recurrence patterns.

The paper was authored by Haoyue Zhang and others, with the latest version dated October 15, 2025 on arXiv (paper ID: 2506.15969).

## R-KV: Redundancy-aware KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Models

Large language models that rely on chain-of-thought or self-reflection produce very long outputs that bloat the key-value cache during inference, and traditional cache-compression schemes tuned for long prompts keep only about 60% of the original accuracy when restricted to 10% of the cache.

### The Solution

R-KV solves this by ranking tokens on-the-fly for both importance and non-redundancy, retaining only the informative, diverse ones. The approach consists of three key components: an attention-based importance scoring mechanism that selects critical tokens for retention, a dynamic redundancy scoring mechanism that identifies repetitive tokens through real-time analysis of key vectors, and a joint eviction mechanism that balances both redundancy and importance to optimize cache efficiency.

### Key Results

The method preserves nearly 100% of the full KV cache performance using only 10% of the KV cache, substantially outperforming existing KV cache baselines, which reach only 60% of the performance. R-KV even achieves 105% of full KV cache performance with 16% of the KV cache, and this KV-cache reduction leads to 90% memory saving and 6.6× throughput over standard chain-of-thought reasoning inference.

### Practical Advantages

R-KV offers up to 90% KV-cache memory savings with zero—sometimes negative—accuracy loss, is a plug-and-play lightweight wrapper for any autoregressive LLM, and is training-free requiring no finetuning.

## PyramidKV and PyramidInfer - Layer-wise KV Cache Budget Allocation

Both PyramidKV and PyramidInfer employ a pyramidal strategy, prioritizing shallower layers with higher cache budgets.

### Key Features:

**PyramidKV:**
This approach dynamically adjusts the KV cache size across different layers, allocating more cache in lower layers and less in higher ones, diverging from traditional methods that maintain a uniform KV cache size.

PyramidKV is motivated by observations that LLMs aggregate information through Pyramidal Information Funneling where attention is scattering widely in lower layers, progressively consolidating within specific contexts, and ultimately focusing on critical tokens in higher layers.

Specifically, PyramidKV allocates more KV cache to the lower layers where information is more dispersed and each KV state contains less information, while reducing the KV cache in higher layers where information becomes concentrated in a few key tokens.

### Performance:

Experimental evaluations using the LongBench benchmark show that PyramidKV matches the performance of models with a full KV cache while retaining only 12% of the KV cache.

### Related Work:

Both PyramidKV (2024) and PyramidInfer (2024) are described as layer-wise budget allocation methods in recent surveys.

## PyramidInfer: Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM Inference

PyramidInfer is a method that compresses the KV cache by layer-wise retaining crucial context. PyramidInfer saves significant memory by computing fewer keys and values without sacrificing performance.

The number of crucial keys and values that influence future generations decreases layer by layer and can be extracted by the consistency in attention weights.

## Overview

KVPress is a comprehensive library enabling researchers to implement and benchmark KV cache compression methods, already including more than 20 techniques.

The library includes multiple compression approaches across different categories:

## Overview

KV cache optimization strategies can be categorized into five major directions: cache eviction, compression and reconstruction, hybrid memory solutions, novel attention mechanisms, and combined approaches.

## Key Methods

**Ada-KV**: Recent efforts aim to reduce KV cache size by evicting vast non-critical cache elements during runtime while preserving generation quality. However, these methods typically allocate compression budgets uniformly across all attention heads, ignoring the unique attention patterns of each head. Adaptive budget allocation across attention heads (AdaKV) significantly improves budget utilization and post-eviction generation quality. Ada-KV was presented at NeurIPS 2025.

**NACL**: NACL is a global optimization method for evicting tokens, combining proxy tokens and random eviction strategies to improve the performance of both long and short text tasks while reducing the KV cache. NACL performs efficient eviction in a single operation during the encoding phase, rather than step-by-step during decoding. This design reduces time complexity and minimizes the computational overhead typically associated with managing large‑scale KV caches.

**Other Notable Methods**: Representative methods such as H2O, SnapKV, and Ada-KV demonstrate the effectiveness of intelligent token selection, while compression techniques like KIVI highlight the potential of quantization.

SkipKV addresses the significant key-value (KV) cache overhead in large reasoning models (LRMs) that grows linearly with verbose chain-of-thought reasoning processes, creating both memory and throughput bottlenecks.

The paper investigates the effectiveness of existing KV cache eviction methods for chain-of-thought reasoning, finding that state-of-the-art eviction methods fail to maintain accuracy in multi-batch settings due to unstable token-wise scoring, and often generate longer sequences than the original model due to semantic-unaware token-wise eviction.

## Overview

H2O (Heavy Hitter Oracle) is a KV cache eviction policy that dynamically retains a balance of recent and H2 tokens. The approach is based on the observation that a small portion of tokens contributes most of the value when computing attention scores, and these tokens are called Heavy Hitters (H2).

## GitHub Repositories

The code is available at https://github.com/FMInference/H2O. Additionally, two implementations are provided: h2o_flexgen for achieving higher throughput for LLM generation (based on FlexGen), and h2o_hf for testing performance on different benchmarks (based on Hugging Face). Both simulation code (masking attention matrix) and real KV dropping implementation are provided.

## KV Cache Implementation

The KV cache is a large amount of transient state information stored in GPU memory that scales linearly with sequence length and batch size, and H2O's approach significantly reduces its memory footprint.

## Performance

H2O with 20% heavy hitters improves throughput over three leading inference systems DeepSpeed Zero-Inference, Hugging Face Accelerate, and FlexGen by up to 29×, 29×, and 3× on OPT-6.7B and OPT-30B.

## FASA GitHub Repository

The code for FASA is available at https://github.com/AMAP-ML/FASA-ICLR2026.

## About FASA

FASA is a novel framework that achieves query-aware token eviction by dynamically predicting token importance. FASA stems from a novel insight into RoPE: the discovery of functional sparsity at the frequency-chunk (FC) level.

Across a spectrum of long-context tasks, from sequence modeling to complex CoT reasoning, FASA consistently outperforms all token-eviction baselines and achieves near-oracle accuracy, demonstrating remarkable robustness even under constraint budgets. ## Overview

LazyEviction is an observation window-based lagged KV eviction scheme integrating recurrence interval tracking. This is a recent research development from 2025.

## Key Components

The framework has two main components:

1. **Recurrence Interval Tracking**: The system records each token's Maximum Recurrence Interval (MRI) — the longest observed period between its attention spikes — to capture the temporal variation of token importance.

2. **MRI-Centric Eviction Policy**: Tokens whose recurrence interval is longer than the time elapsed since their last attention are retained as they still have the potential to become important in the future.

LazyEviction has been implemented on large reasoning models ranging from 4B to 32B parameters, and has been verified to maintain comparable performance while reducing 50%~70% KV budget, surpassing state-of-the-art KV cache compression methods.

## Repository Overview

SnapKV is an innovative and out-of-box KV cache compression method. The official repository is located at https://github.com/FasterDecoding/SnapKV.

## Implementation Details

The project is currently tested with transformers==4.37.0, with compatibility for higher versions needing to be checked. 

The detailed algorithm of SnapKV is in snapkv_utils.py, and currently the project supports Llama family, Mistral, and Mixtral models.

## How It Works

The fundamental approach involves identifying and selecting the most crucial attention features per head to create the new KV cache, selecting important features based on the observation window (the last segment of the prompt), concatenating selected features with window features containing all prompt information, then storing the concatenated KV caches for later use in generation.

## Integration

SnapKV uses monkey patches to enable the functionality (such as replace_mistral()), can be easily integrated with other models, and follows comments marked with [SnapKV] in existing models to construct your own.

## Performance

At a sequence length of 16k and batch size of 2, SnapKV achieves approximately a 3.6x speedup compared to baseline, with decoding time consistently remaining below 40 ms.

## PyramidKV Method

PyramidKV is a novel and effective KV cache compression method that dynamically adjusts the KV cache size across different layers, allocating more cache in lower layers and less in higher ones, diverging from traditional methods that maintain a uniform KV cache size.

## NACL: A General and Effective KV Cache Eviction Framework for LLMs

NACL is a general framework for long-context KV cache eviction that achieves more optimal and efficient eviction in a single operation during the encoding phase.

### Key Components

The framework combines two main strategies:

1. **Proxy-Tokens Eviction**: Proxy tokens are selected from the question input, commonly located at the end of a long text, and are more capable of retaining the task-specific tokens in KV cache.

2. **Random Eviction**: Random Eviction is incorporated into Proxy-Tokens Eviction to randomly sample tokens to evict from the probability distribution in Proxy-Tokens Eviction with different seed on attention heads and layers.

### Purpose and Benefits

The approach combines more accurate attention score statistics in Proxy Tokens Eviction with the diversified random eviction strategy of Random Eviction, aiming to alleviate the issue of attention bias and enhance the robustness in maintaining pivotal tokens for long-context modeling tasks.

The method significantly improves performance on short- and long-text tasks by 80% and 76% respectively, reducing KV Cache by up to 50% with over 95% performance maintenance.

The paper was published at ACL 2024 in Bangkok, Thailand in August 2024.

## KeyDiff Overview

KeyDiff is a training-free KV cache eviction method based on key similarity. KeyDiffPress evicts tokens based solely on key similarity.

## Core Concept

The method demonstrates that geometrically distinctive keys during LLM inference tend to have high attention scores, and is based on this phenomenon. Unlike other KV cache eviction methods, KeyDiff does not rely on attention scores, allowing the use of optimized attention mechanisms like FlashAttention.

## Theoretical Basis

KeyDiff computes the optimal solution for an optimization problem minimizing the pairwise cosine similarity among keys in the KV cache.

## Performance Results

KeyDiff significantly outperforms state-of-the-art KV cache eviction methods under similar memory constraints, with only a 1.5% and 0.04% accuracy drop from the non-evicting baseline while achieving 33% and 23% KV cache memory reduction on LongBench. Additionally, it decreases end-to-end inference latency by up to 30% compared to other token-eviction methods.

## Expected Attention and KVPress

Expected Attention is a training-free compression method that estimates KV pairs importance by predicting how future queries will attend to them.

### Key Technical Approach

The approach leverages the distributional properties of LLM activations to compute expected attention scores in closed form for each KV pair. These scores enable principled ranking and pruning of KV pairs with minimal impact on the residual stream, achieving effective compression without performance degradation.

### Performance and Applicability

The method operates seamlessly across both prefilling and decoding phases, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in both scenarios.

### KVPress Library

KVPress is a comprehensive library that enables researchers to implement and benchmark KV cache compression methods, already including more than 20 techniques. The library includes multiple compression methods such as ObservedAttentionPress, which uses "average attention weight observed during in prefilling phase."

The paper was published on arXiv on October 1, 2025 (arXiv:2510.00636) with authors Alessio Devoto, Maximilian Jeblick, and Simon Jégou.     title: "H₂O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models"
    authors: "Zhenyu Zhang, Ying Sheng, Tianyi Zhou, Tianlong Chen, Lianmin Zheng, Ruisi Cai, Zhao Song, Yuandong Tian, Christopher Ré, Clark Barrett, Zhangyang Wang, Beidi Chen"
    year: 2023
    venue: NeurIPS 2023
    arxiv: "2306.14048"
    core_mechanism: >
      基于 Heavy Hitter 观察：少量 token 贡献了大部分 attention score。
      维护 cumulative attention score，动态保留 recent tokens + top-scored Heavy Hitter tokens。
      eviction 公式化为 dynamic submodular 问题，有理论保证。
    time_complexity: "O(B) per token (维护 cumulative score + greedy eviction)"
    calibration_required: false
    evaluation:
      metrics: [PPL, throughput, downstream accuracy]
      results: >
        20% heavy hitters 即可保持接近 full-cache 性能。
        OPT-6.7B/30B 上 throughput 提升 29x (vs Accelerate), 3x (vs FlexGen)。

    diff_from_ours: >
      H2O 用 cumulative attention score 做 scoring，O(B) 但需要完整 attention matrix。
      我们用 EMA centroid similarity 做 O(1) scoring，不依赖 attention score，
      可兼容 FlashAttention。

    year: 2023
    venue: ICLR 2024
    arxiv: "2309.17453"
    core_mechanism: >
      发现 attention sink 现象：初始 token 即使语义无关也获得极高 attention score。
      保留 sink tokens (前几个 token) + sliding window of recent tokens，
      丢弃中间 tokens。极其简单但有效的 streaming baseline。
    time_complexity: "O(1) per token (固定 window size，无 scoring 计算)"
    calibration_required: false

      StreamingLLM 完全丢弃中间 token 的 KV，不做 importance scoring。
      适合纯 streaming 场景但对长距离依赖支持差。

      eviction 公式化为 dynamic submodular 问题，有理论保证。

    calibration_required: false

    title: "KeyDiff: Key Similarity-Based KV Cache Eviction for Long-Context LLM Inference"
    authors: "Junyoung Park, Dalton Jones, Matthew J Morse, Raghavv Goel, Mingu Lee, Chris Lott"
    year: 2025
    venue: NeurIPS 2025
    arxiv: "2504.15364"
    core_mechanism: >
      基于 key geometric distinctiveness：geometrically distinctive keys 有高 attention score。
      不依赖 attention score，仅用 key vector 间 cosine similarity。
      最小化 KV cache 中 keys 的 pairwise cosine similarity。
      兼容 FlashAttention（不需要 attention matrix）。
    time_complexity: "O(B²) per eviction step (pairwise cosine similarity)"
    calibration_required: false
    evaluation:
      metrics: [LongBench accuracy, memory reduction, latency]
      results: >
        33% KV memory 减少下仅 1.5% accuracy drop。
        端到端 latency 降低 30%。
    diff_from_ours: >
      KeyDiff 与我们思路最相近——都用 key similarity 而非 attention score。
      但 KeyDiff 用 pairwise similarity (O(B²))，我们用 EMA centroid (O(1))。
      KeyDiff 是我们最直接的技术 baseline。
    code: null  # kvpress 内有实现
    kvpress_support: true  # kvpress v0.5.3 内置 KeyDiffPress

  ExpectedAttention:
    title: "Expected Attention: KV Cache Compression by Estimating Attention from Future Queries Distribution"
    authors: "Alessio Devoto, Maximilian Jeblick, Simon Jégou"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv preprint"
    arxiv: "2510.00636"
    core_mechanism: >
      利用 LLM activation 的分布性质，closed-form 计算每个 KV pair 的 expected attention score。
      预测未来 query 对当前 KV 的 attention，无需实际 future query。
      同时适用于 prefilling 和 decoding 阶段。
    time_complexity: "O(B·d) per token (d=head dim, closed-form 计算)"
    calibration_required: false
    evaluation:
      metrics: [LongBench, PPL, prefill+decode compression]
      results: >
        在 prefill 和 decode 两个阶段都超越 SOTA baselines。
    diff_from_ours: >
      ExpectedAttention 基于 distributional assumption 预测 future attention。
      我们用 EMA centroid 做 empirical importance tracking，更简单直接。
      ExpectedAttention 需要 O(B·d)，我们 O(1)。
    code: null  # kvpress 内有实现
    kvpress_support: true  # kvpress v0.5.3 内置 ExpectedAttentionPress
